paper_title: Quantum teleportation implies symmetry-protected topological order
authors: Yifan Hong; David T. Stephen; Aaron J. Friedman
source_locator: Explicit open question on PDF page 10
statement: e parity (−1)n . project onto states of Ω with Z As far as we are aware, the recovery operations of all physical teleportation protocols known to the literature are Clifford in the sense of Def. 5. We also preclude outcome-dependent measurements, which are not only higher-order Clifford [3] on Hdil (14), but are generally not useful to physical teleportation on their own or in combination with the Clifford recovery channels of Def. 5. Essentially, conditional measurements fail to preserve crucial properties of the logical operators (e.g., unitarity). As an aside, we conjecture that physical teleportation protocols can be classified according to their recovery group—the set generated by the recovery operators χΩ for in the recovery channels RΩ (34) in W (31) under multiplication. That group is equivalent to the set of all possible byproduct operators. Restricting to the Clifford recovery channels of Def. 5, the recovery group must be a subset of the Pauli group Pph . Since the phase of the logical states |ψn ⟩ is unimportant, we have X Z ∼ = Z X , so that the recovery group is effectively Abelian. Since Pph also spans all physical operators, this is likely the simplest nontrivial recovery group that can realize. We relegate the consideration of more complicated recovery channels (and groups) to future work.
